historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; reads the field but lacks structure applicability, zero/unspecified handling and exact enclosure provenance.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; correctly excludes power manipulation but conflates approved topology input with manual core execution.

original_test_intent: Verify the Number Of Power Cords metadata in the intended SMBIOS Type 3 enclosure record matches the approved chassis input-power design or an explicitly supported unspecified value and remains stable after reboot, without manipulating any cord.
original_method: Capture complete Type 3 records, bind the enclosure by serial/asset/type/BOM, extract the raw and decoded cord-count byte, compare it with the approved enclosure power-entry baseline and applicability rule, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the expected count/topology or supported-unspecified policy and reboot plan. The metadata collection and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Approved Type 3 power-cord count or supported-unspecified value
Definition of what the count represents for the enclosure power-entry design
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not insert, remove, cycle or re-route AC cords under this case.
Preserve complete Type 3 output and raw count; do not infer current connected-cord or redundancy state from static metadata.
Do not assume PSU module count, inlet count and external cord count are interchangeable.
Do not accept zero/unspecified without approved applicability and do not assume the first Type 3 record.
Stop on ambiguity, unexpected count, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect all Type 3 structures, bind the enclosure and compare raw/decoded Number Of Power Cords with the approved input-power model before/after reboot.
Do not manipulate power, claim redundancy/failover coverage, modify DMI or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the count semantics, enclosure power-entry baseline and zero/applicability policy.
Resolve discrepancies among external cords, inlets and PSU modules and issue the verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The decoded label is relevant, but grep loses raw byte, enclosure identity and applicability, suppresses errors and assumes insecure transport.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete Type 3 output/tool/errors, select the enclosure through correlated identity and retain both raw and decoded cord-count values.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Number Of Power Cords field, Type 3 script and 5/5-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Verify structure-version applicability, bind the enclosure, compare the raw cord-count byte and decoded value against a project definition that distinguishes cords, inlets and PSU modules, and govern zero explicitly across reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 3 records whose version/formatted length includes Number Of Power Cords.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, dmidecode, BIOS, enclosure and power-topology/BOM revisions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 3 Number Of Power Cords semantics, approved chassis power architecture and installed dmidecode documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds count semantics, raw/applicability evidence and strict separation from live redundancy testing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; power-cord removal and redundancy behavior remain separate high-risk coverage.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Expected count definition and supported-zero policy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Static firmware metadata does not prove how many cords are presently connected or whether redundancy functions.

project_override_considerations: A project may accept zero/unspecified when the field is unsupported or define the count at enclosure inlet level, but must document that model and cannot claim physical connection/redundancy validation.
expected_evidence: Approval, count semantics/baseline, applicability, enclosure mapping and tool/SMBIOS versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 3 record plus raw/decoded count comparison
Engineer verdict and separate redundancy-test reference if applicable

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and criteria consistently target the static Type 3 count; absent project count semantics do not create contradictory instructions.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The field is safely readable and identifiable; count definition and expected value are readiness inputs.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds raw count, applicability and enclosure provenance.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps the no-power-manipulation boundary while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Distinguishes cords, inlets, PSU modules and connected-state/redundancy semantics and formalizes zero handling.

review_improvement: Prevents a static field from being mistaken for current connection or failover evidence and avoids unsafe cord manipulation within this metadata row.
independent_technical_reasoning: After the project defines the count and enclosure mapping, the entire read/compare/reboot workflow is software-controlled; supplying topology does not make it PARTIAL.
